newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise's Sedgwick/West Brae get go-ahead.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise's Sedgwick/West Brae get go-ahead.

text.p: Enterprise Oil Plc said on Wednesday the UK government has approved the joint development, with Marathon Oil UK Ltd, of the Sedgwick and West Brae North Sea fields.
The development calls for a single Sedgwick production well to be tied back 2.3 km to the West Brae subsea manifold.

The commingled flow will be piped to the Marathon-operated Brae 'A' platform for processing and then passed through the Brae and Forties pipeline systems. Production is to be split 67.5 percent to Brae and 32.5 percent to Sedgwick.
Reserves are expected to exceed 40 million barrels with first production expected in the fourth quarter of 1997 at an initial 30,000 barrels per day and at an average 27,000 bpd thereafter.
Joint development costs will be around 100 million stg, Enterprise said in a statement.
The Sedgwick and West Brae drilling programme will be carried out by semi-submersible drilling rig, Transocean Explorer, starting this month.
